ops.title: Decide the fate of gitPushRejected's [remote rejected] veto — correct but unreachable
ops.description:
`internal/cli/shippush.go`'s `gitPushRejected` vetoes on `[remote rejected]`
before matching `(non-fast-forward)`/`(fetch first)`. Its stated rationale — "a
multi-ref push can mix a non-FF ref with a hook-declined ref" — was MEASURED
correct (2026-08-03): one `git push origin a b` really does emit both tokens in
one stderr, and the veto's effect is real. Without it, a hook-declined push is
wrapped as `*pushRejectedError` and `shipPushRetry` re-enters up to
`shipPushAttempts = 3`, doing three real fetch+rebase cycles against a hook that
declines deterministically, then blaming a race for a policy decline.

**But ccx cannot reach that state.** Every git push ccx issues is single-ref:
`ship.go:1262`, `:1270` (the `--force-with-lease` push), `:1304`; no `--tags`, no
`--follow-tags`, no refspec list, and an explicit refspec overrides `push.default`.
The jj lane pushes one bookmark (`ship.go:1193`); the gt lane submits through gt.
A single-ref push emits one rejection line, and in the single-ref hook-decline
case the veto is REDUNDANT — the captured stderr carries `[remote rejected]` with
no `(non-fast-forward)`/`(fetch first)` anywhere, so the function already returns
false without it.

So it is a guard against a state ccx's own argv cannot represent, which this
repo's style rules normally delete — but it is one correct line that becomes live
the moment anything pushes two refs, and no test can exercise it through ccx's
public surface, so the converted suite will never cover it either.

Options: (a) delete it per the no-guards rule; (b) keep it and pin the invariant
instead with a test asserting every push argv ccx builds names exactly one ref,
so adding `--tags` later fails loudly and points at this decision; (c) keep as-is
with a comment recording the unreachability.

Related unmeasured pairing: `gitPushStaleLease` has NO veto, so if a hook decline
can co-occur with a `(stale info)` lease rejection, it would misclassify the
decline as a stale lease. Same single-ref unreachability argument applies, but the
pairing itself was never measured.

ops.text: A decision is recorded: delete the veto, or keep it with the single-ref invariant pinned by a test over ccx's push argv
